falsifier: A keep on do_players (or any function with a surplus callee-saved register) that closes a per-cluster structural residual and RAISES fresh objdiff fuzzy without changing the save set. Run `python tools/gdl/savedregs.py game/game/player do_players --uses` to read the assignment in both streams, and re-check the save-set delta with `fnasm.py game/game/player do_players 0x8:0x18 --diff`; if the delta has closed, this law's premise is gone and every probe listed above should be re-run at the new alignment.
subject: function:do_players
value: When our object saves one MORE callee-saved GPR than the target (do_players: ours `stmw r15,140(r1)` / frame 264 against target `stmw r16,136(r1)` / frame 256), every register number in the body is shifted, so an edit that closes real named structure at ONE site re-rolls the allocation everywhere and loses more fuzzy than the site gains. Five probes across two runs now share this exact signature on do_players and not one of them is a keep: probe A closes both j-loop twins (multiset 14t -> 12t) at 97.2692 -> 96.8433; probes I and J reach EXACT instruction count T1174/O1174 with multiset 12t at 96.8458 and 96.9055; probe N deletes a genuine redundant load and reads 96.7112; probe O reproduces the target's add / displacement-load / addi trio byte-for-byte at +0x10e0 and reads 96.7155. The operational rule is a PRIORITY, not a prohibition: on such a function the save set is the first residual to work and per-cluster structure is the last, because until the surplus register is shed no per-cluster win can survive arbitration — and correspondingly, a probe on such a function that improves fuzzy WITHOUT touching a long-lived value (do_players PROBE M, a compare operand-order swap: real 840 -> 836, count held, 97.2692 -> 97.2862) is the shape of edit that does pay.
